items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: Bro happened to be playing that, and he was playing bass violin, but all the rest of the band was playing tubas.

ctx.x: No, I don't remember anybody playing four on the slow blues. I'll tell you another thing, when I went to New York everybody was playing tuba in a regular dance band. You know what we were with stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff

they'd use a string bass. I was surprised to see them, but one band I think that I knew that was using a string band, that was Duke Hamilton. Bro happened to be playing that, and he was playing bass violin, but all the rest of the band was playing tubas.
Did they use banjos much here?

items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: That's where Hall came from. Hall's father was a clown that played.

ctx.x: Dance bands, brass bands, show bands, you know, tent shows, art, and the medicine show and art. They got to have a little bit different tempos. Could you explain that? Well, they do have different tempos.

They have what they call six-eighth time. They have what they call to play some in two full time. See what I mean? Well, who would use those? Well, brass bands, like a minister band, they use six-eighth time for the street. You understand? And some tunes, they used two full times. And some tunes, yeah, two full times, like Sally Trombone, that was a great street number, because there was plenty of trombone in there. You remember that? There had plenty of trombone in there. Yeah. They have two trombones in the…
This is the young dog. Mr. Brooke was on this, then. Let's start it again. Yeah, go ahead. The very beginning.
